target.purpose: Require every natural-language data claim to bind exact claim identity to unique registered query citations and the exact accepted query registry before passing the citation gate.
target.central_bottleneck: A citation ID without claim identity or registry identity cannot establish which statement and which accepted query namespace were actually checked, while missing/duplicate/unknown citations can make audit trails ambiguous.
success: Empty claims and absent citations refuse.
Empty, duplicate, and unknown query citations refuse.
Citation order is canonicalized for claim identity.
Exact claim text and unique citation set are fingerprinted.
Accepted query registry identity is independently fingerprinted.
Every result binds claim identity, registry identity, citations, and refusal evidence.
The public claim remains citation registration rather than semantic entailment.

invariants: one or more unique non-empty citations
every citation must exist in accepted registry
citation order does not change canonical claim identity
claim identity and registry identity are receipt-bound
registered citation does not imply semantic support

donors.boundary: future full query-intent fingerprints may replace the current query-ID registry, but no integration is yet exercised

evolution.composition_gate: Do not claim query-intent integration or result-to-claim semantic support until executable receipt binding is independently proven.

nonclaims: not a production Snowflake Cortex claim service
no query execution or result verification
